periods.section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
periods.activity_title: Reading Bibha Chowdhuri's Story Aloud and in Discussion

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us read (p.233): paired word-web on qualities of a scientist.
Let us discuss (p.237): arrange key life events in chronological order.

time_bands.activity: Students work in pairs to complete the word-web of qualities they associate with a scientist, then share responses with the class. This activates prior knowledge and frames the profile that follows.

Teacher reads the informational text aloud (p.232–239) with students following in their books; teacher pauses at key moments — Bibha joining the Bose Institute, her move to Manchester, the pi-meson discovery — inviting brief oral responses.
Students individually arrange six events from Bibha Chowdhuri's life in correct chronological order (p.237), then compare with a partner before a whole-class check led by the teacher.

periods.teacher_notes: The word-web opener works well when students are asked to justify each quality — this surfaces assumptions about gender in science that the text later challenges. A common pitfall is treating chronological sequencing as a memory task rather than a reading comprehension task; prompt students to return to the text to locate dates and signal words before arranging the events.

periods.section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
periods.activity_title: Extract Analysis and Critical Reading of Bibha's Legacy

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us discuss (p.237–238): four questions on Extract 1 — Manchester and cosmic rays.
Let us think and reflect (p.238–239): two questions — pioneer status and Schrödinger nomination.

homework.task_brief: Let us discuss (p.238): four questions on Extract 2 — Bibha's enduring legacy.

time_bands.activity: Teacher briefly revisits the chronological sequence of Bibha's life constructed around her Manchester years and the pi-meson discovery, using student responses to frame the extract work ahead.

Students read Extract 1 (p.237–238) silently, then work through the four questions — on Blackett's significance, public perception of women scientists, the meaning of 'celebrated,' and the idiom 'an eye for' — in pairs before whole-class discussion.

Teacher leads a guided discussion on two questions from 'Let us think and reflect' (p.238–239): why Bibha is considered a pioneer, and what Schrödinger's nomination reveals about her abilities. Students write brief responses in their notebooks before sharing.

periods.teacher_notes: Students often misread 'celebrated' as meaning 'someone who celebrates'; directing them to substitute candidate synonyms (renowned, famous, well-regarded) and test each against the sentence sharpens word-choice reasoning. The Schrödinger question rewards students who can distinguish evidence of ability from evidence of institutional recognition — a distinction the prose explicitly makes about Bibha's unawarded decades.

periods.section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
periods.activity_title: AI Podcast Listening and Mobile Phone Panel Discussion

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us listen (p.244): five MCQs on the AI podcast — healthcare, environment, education, accessibility.
Let us speak (p.244–245): panel discussion on mobile phones — five assigned roles.

time_bands.activity: Teacher introduces the podcast context: students will hear a segment called Tech Talks on artificial intelligence and must listen for specific claims about four sectors. Students prepare a rough answer grid.

Teacher reads the Tech Talks podcast transcript (p.251–252) aloud at a measured pace; students listen and select correct answers to the five multiple-choice questions about AI in healthcare, environment, education, and accessibility. Answers are checked as a class.

Groups of five conduct the panel discussion on 'Evaluating the Impact of Mobile Phones — Beneficial or Harmful,' each student taking one role (Moderator, Principal, Teacher, Parent, Student) using the cue prompts. The teacher circulates and closes with brief whole-class reflection on how well different perspectives were represented.

periods.teacher_notes: Reading the transcript at a natural podcast pace — slightly faster than a read-aloud — is more authentic than reading slowly; this is good preparation for real listening tasks. In the panel discussion, students who are quieter by nature often flourish when their role (e.g. Moderator) carries a structural function rather than requiring them to argue a position — assigning roles thoughtfully can open participation.

periods.section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
periods.activity_title: Science Exhibition Report and Vocabulary in Context

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us write (p.246): formal magazine report on Zonal Science Exhibition — headline, name, three paragraphs.
Let us learn (p.240): add suffixes -ship, -ment, -hood to eight root words.

homework.task_brief: Let us learn (p.240): substitute underlined phrases with words from the box — physicist, peers, luminaries, barriers, pioneers, persistence.

time_bands.activity: Teacher puts the report format on the board — headline, byline, three paragraphs — and models the opening sentence using passive voice and third person, drawing on the cues provided in 'Let us write' (p.246).

Students draft the full magazine report independently, using the cue list (organiser, date, Chief Guest, competitions, winning team, observations) and applying past tense and passive voice throughout. Teacher circulates to provide formative feedback on format and voice. Students exchange drafts with a partner for a quick peer read before revising.

Students complete the suffix activity from 'Let us learn' (p.240), adding -ship, -ment, or -hood to each of the eight root words and writing the complete word in their notebooks. Two or three responses are shared and discussed as a class to confirm patterns.

periods.teacher_notes: The most common error in this report task is slipping into first-person or active voice mid-paragraph; a brief reminder to check each verb before the peer-read step helps students catch this themselves. The suffix activity connects naturally to vocabulary met in the Bibha Chowdhuri profile — 'professorship,' 'mentorship,' 'leadership' — which gives students a living example to anchor each pattern. The word-substitution vocabulary task (physicist, peers, luminaries) is assigned as self-study since context-matching is well-suited to individual review.

periods.section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
periods.activity_title: Passive Voice in Context and Women Pioneers Exploration

tasks_in_class.task_brief: Let us learn (p.242): complete news report using passive forms of six verbs — discover, test, measure, publish, record, take.
Let us explore (p.251): read about and discuss women pioneers from different fields in India.

time_bands.activity: Teacher briefly revisits the active-to-passive transformation introduced in the text alongside the sentence about Bibha's pioneering role, establishing the grammatical pattern students will apply.

Students complete the news report passage on the malaria vaccine (p.242) by filling in the passive forms of the six given verbs, then compare answers with a partner. The teacher leads a class check, drawing attention to tense choices — was + past participle — and any irregular past participles.

Students read the 'Let us explore' section on women pioneers from different fields in India (p.251) and participate in a structured discussion: each student names one scientist and identifies one barrier she overcame, connecting themes from Bibha Chowdhuri's profile to contemporary women in STEM. The teacher closes by drawing together threads about how persistence and institutional support both matter.

periods.teacher_notes: Students frequently confuse 'was published' with 'has been published' when the time reference is a specific past event — the news report context (last year) makes it possible to demonstrate clearly why simple past passive is correct here. The women pioneers discussion is richest when students move beyond naming achievements to identifying what structural barriers each woman faced, echoing the critical reading of Bibha's own unawarded decades.

items.source_section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
items.source_lo: Student identifies and sequences key biographical events using an informational text as the vehicle.
items.source_context: Bibha Chowdhuri's life: Bose Institute, Manchester, pi-meson discovery, TIFR, Nobel nomination, star renaming.
items.item_stem:
Read the following events from Bibha Chowdhuri's life. Which of the following correctly places her nomination for the Nobel Prize by Erwin Schrödinger in relation to her work at the University of Manchester?
A. The nomination came before she travelled to Manchester.
B. The nomination came after she returned to India and joined TIFR.
C. The nomination came while she was still studying under Patrick Blackett in Manchester.
D. The nomination came after the International Astronomical Union renamed a star in her honour.

options.label: A
options.text: The nomination came after she returned to India and joined TIFR.

options.label: B
options.text: The nomination came after the International Astronomical Union renamed a star in her honour.

options.label: C
options.text: The nomination came before she travelled to Manchester.

options.label: D
options.text: The nomination came while she was still studying under Patrick Blackett in Manchester.

what_each_option_reveals.C: Suggests the student has not tracked the sequence — Manchester (1945–1949) precedes the nomination (1950).
what_each_option_reveals.D: Conflates her time in Manchester with the nomination year 1950, after her return to India.
what_each_option_reveals.B: Confuses the 2019 star-renaming with the 1950 nomination, reversing the chronology by nearly seventy years.

items.source_section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
items.source_lo: Student identifies and sequences key biographical events using an informational text as the vehicle.
items.source_context: Bibha Chowdhuri's life: Bose Institute, Manchester, pi-meson discovery, TIFR, Nobel nomination, star renaming.
items.item_stem: Bibha Chowdhuri's career moved through several institutions and countries. In a short paragraph of three to four sentences, describe the sequence of her institutional affiliations from the Bose Institute to the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, explaining what each move represented in her scientific journey.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: Bibha Chowdhuri began at the Bose Institute in Kolkata, where she established herself as India's first woman physicist. She then moved to the University of Manchester (1945) to deepen her research in cosmic rays under Patrick Blackett, leading to her pi-meson discovery. On returning to India in 1949, she joined TIFR as its first woman faculty member, later working at the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad under Vikram Sarabhai and finally at the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics in Kolkata.

items.source_section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
items.source_lo: Student interprets language choices and infers authorial intent by critically reading an informational text.
items.source_context: Extract analysis: Blackett's significance, press framing of women scientists, idiomatic language, legacy claims.
items.item_stem:
The press described Bibha Chowdhuri as "India's New Woman Scientist — She has an eye for Cosmic Rays." Which of the following best explains what the use of the word "New" in this headline suggests about attitudes towards women scientists in the 1940s?
A. Women scientists had always been common in India and Bibha was the latest in a long line.
B. Bibha had recently changed her area of scientific research from biology to physics.
C. The idea of an Indian woman excelling in physics was novel enough to be newsworthy.
D. Newspapers at the time regularly celebrated scientists with new discoveries.

options.label: A
options.text: Bibha had recently changed her area of scientific research from biology to physics.

options.label: B
options.text: Newspapers at the time regularly celebrated scientists with new discoveries.

options.label: C
options.text: The idea of an Indian woman excelling in physics was novel enough to be newsworthy.

options.label: D
options.text: Women scientists had always been common in India and Bibha was the latest in a long line.

what_each_option_reveals.D: Contradicts the text's central argument that Bibha was a trailblazer precisely because women in physics were rare.
what_each_option_reveals.A: Introduces a biographical detail not present in the text; conflates the word 'New' with a change of field.
what_each_option_reveals.B: Treats the headline as routine rather than reading it as a marker of social surprise — the student misses the gendered dimension.

items.source_section_title: Bibha Chowdhuri — The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science
items.source_lo: Student interprets language choices and infers authorial intent by critically reading an informational text.
items.source_context: Extract analysis: Blackett's significance, press framing of women scientists, idiomatic language, legacy claims.
items.item_stem: The author of this profile chooses to end by connecting Bibha Chowdhuri's "quiet determination" to the over fifty women who contributed to Chandrayaan-3 and to Dr. Ritu Karidhal Srivastava. What does this structural choice reveal about the author's purpose in writing the text? Support your response with at least one specific detail from the profile.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: The author uses this connection to argue that Bibha Chowdhuri's perseverance created a foundation for today's women in Indian science, making her legacy tangible rather than symbolic. By naming Dr. Ritu Karidhal Srivastava and the Chandrayaan-3 team, the author shows that Bibha's "quiet determination" produced measurable, ongoing outcomes — not just historical recognition.

items.item_stem:
In the Tech Talks podcast, which of the following correctly describes what AI did during the global pandemic?
A. AI robots monitored patient behaviour in hospitals.
B. AI assisted in speeding up the discovery of new medicines.
C. AI developed different types of vaccines independently.

options.label: A
options.text: AI assisted in speeding up the discovery of new medicines.

options.label: B
options.text: AI developed different types of vaccines independently.

options.label: C
options.text: AI robots monitored patient behaviour in hospitals.

what_each_option_reveals.C: Confuses AI-assisted surgery (a separate point) with pandemic-specific applications; the podcast does not state robots monitored patient behaviour.
what_each_option_reveals.B: Overstates AI's role — the podcast says AI 'sped up discovery,' not that AI developed vaccines by itself.

items.source_lo: Student extends word knowledge by applying derivational suffixes to form new words from root words.
items.source_context: Suffix -ship, -ment, -hood added to: member, govern, partner, child, citizen, entertain, brother, agree; modelled on professorship, mentorship, leadership.
items.item_stem: The profile of Bibha Chowdhuri mentions that Homi J. Bhabha offered her mentorship at TIFR, and the Government of India later declared a chair professorship in her name. Both words — mentorship and professorship — use the suffix -ship to mean 'the state or condition of.' Using this pattern, write a sentence of your own for TWO of the following words: citizenship, partnership, agreement. Your sentences must show that you understand what each word means.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: Acceptable responses show clear understanding of meaning, e.g.: 'Bibha's citizenship in India gave her the right to return and contribute to national institutions like TIFR.' / 'The partnership between Vikram Sarabhai and Bibha Chowdhuri at the Physical Research Laboratory advanced cosmic ray research.' / 'Both scientists signed an agreement to share their experimental data with the wider research community.'

items.item_stem:
Fill in the blanks in the following short news report about a science achievement, using the correct passive form of each verb given in brackets.

Last month, a new method for purifying water 1. __________ (develop) by a team of researchers in India. The method 2. __________ (test) in three different laboratories before its results 3. __________ (publish) in an international journal. Water samples from ten rivers 4. __________ (collect) for the study, and the levels of harmful bacteria 5. __________ (measure) carefully at each stage.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: 1. was developed  2. was tested  3. were published  4. were collected  5. were measured

items.item_stem:
The Bibha Chowdhuri profile states that 'the foundation was laid by early pioneers.' This sentence uses the passive voice to shift focus from the doer to the action and its result. Rewrite the following two active sentences about Bibha's achievements in the passive voice, keeping the meaning the same.

1. Erwin Schrödinger nominated Bibha Chowdhuri for the Nobel Prize in 1950.
2. The International Astronomical Union renamed a star in the constellation Leo as 'Bibha' in 2019.

teacher_guide.suggested_answer: 1. Bibha Chowdhuri was nominated for the Nobel Prize by Erwin Schrödinger in 1950. 2. A star in the constellation Leo was renamed 'Bibha' by the International Astronomical Union in 2019.

items.item_stem: The profile of Bibha Chowdhuri argues that her persistence in the face of institutional barriers laid the foundation for women in Indian science today. Choose ONE woman pioneer from a field other than physics — such as medicine, space research, or another STEM area — and write a paragraph of five to six sentences explaining one specific barrier she faced and how she overcame it. Connect her experience to at least one challenge Bibha Chowdhuri also encountered.

expected_elements: Names a specific woman pioneer from a field other than physics.
Identifies one clear, specific barrier she faced.
Explains how she overcame or navigated that barrier.
Draws an explicit connection to a challenge from Bibha Chowdhuri's life.

items.source_context: Women pioneers from different fields in India; connection to Bibha Chowdhuri's barriers and persistence; contemporary STEM role models.
items.item_stem: Design a research project titled 'Unsung Women of Indian Science.' Your project should: (a) identify at least three women scientists from India whose contributions are not widely known, (b) describe for each one the field she worked in and one discovery or achievement she made, and (c) propose one creative way — such as a podcast episode, a classroom display, or a short documentary outline — in which your school could help more people learn about their work. Write a plan of six to eight sentences outlining what you would do and why.

expected_elements: Names at least three Indian women scientists from less widely known fields.
States one discovery or achievement for each scientist named.
Proposes a specific, feasible creative outreach format.
Explains clearly why the chosen format would reach a wider audience.
